sentences.text:
Author: Rajesh Bindal
Bench: Rajesh Bindal
 1
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal No. /2025
Raj Rani & Anr. App
VERSUS  THE STATE OF PUNJAB & ANR. Res  O R D E R Leave granted.

The appellants have been arraigned as accused for the offences punishable under Sections 323, 406,
498A, 417, 201 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

The only issue for consideration is as to whether the counsel appearing for the appellants before the High Court, made the submission that the appellants were willing to deposit a sum of Rs.5 lakhs each, to be kept in the form of FDR, on instructions or not.
Learned counsel appearing for the appellants herein submits that no such instruction had been given, as the appellants were and are not in a position to comply with the same.
This position is disputed by the respondent who appears in person before us.

In such view of the matter, we are inclined to Reason: set aside the impugned order, as anticipatory bail has been granted based on the submission of the counsel appearing for the appellants therein,
and therefore, merits have not been gone into by the High Court.
Accordingly, the impugned order is set aside and the matter stands remitted to the High Court for fresh consideration.
Till the disposal of the anticipatory bail application, the appellants shall not be arrested subject to their cooperation with the trial.
The appeals stand allowed, accordingly.
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

Till the disposal of the anticipatory bail application, the appellants shall not be arrested subject to their cooperation with the trial.

The appeals stand allowed,
